when_charged.note: Outcome trading only charges fees when closing or settling, not when opening; only fee-paying volume counts.

rebates.note: Outcome trading does not support rebates; users who would get rebates pay zero fees on maker orders.

tick.unverified: No tick or price precision rule for outcomes is stated on the HIP-4, asset ID or tick and lot size pages.

merged_book.note: Buying Yes at p is equivalent to selling No at 1 - p; at the same merged price level, resting sells sort before resting dual buys.

decimals.unverified: No size decimals rule for outcomes is stated on the pages read.

collateral.note: Outcomes are fully collateralized and involve no leverage or liquidations.

yes_payout.note: Yes converts to settleFraction quote tokens per token; 1 for binary yes, 0 for binary no.

recurring_binary.note: The first market is a recurring binary that settles daily at 06:00 UTC to the BTC mark price.

binary_rule.note: Settles Yes when the mark price interpolated at the settlement time is at or above the target; t0 and t1 are the mark updates just before and after.

bucket_rule.value: three buckets: < P1, [P1, P2), >= P2; exactly one settles to 1
bucket_rule.note: class:priceBucket, using the same interpolated price.

sides.note: Sides are labeled by sideSpecs in outcomeMeta, often Yes and No. Asset encoding = 10 * outcome + side.

split_merge.note: Users may split and merge outcomes to convert between primary and dual balances.

questions.note: In a question exactly one outcome settles Yes; outcomes are linked by negate and merge, so No shares across a question can be redeemed before settlement.

multi_outcome.note: Multi-outcome markets will be supported but are not part of the initial mainnet release.

rebate_payment.note: Maker rebates are paid out continuously on each trade directly to the trading wallet.

liquidation_fee.note: Unlike CEXs there is no clearance fee on liquidations.

max_significant_figures.note: Integer prices are always allowed, regardless of significant figures.

max_price_decimals.note: MAX_DECIMALS is 6 for perps. szDecimals comes from each asset's meta.

decimals.note: Sizes are rounded to the szDecimals of the asset, found in the meta response of the info endpoint.

max_leverage.note: Leverage can be any integer between 1 and the asset's max leverage. The liquidations page says max leverage varies from 3x to 40x.

initial_margin.note: Initial margin fraction; margin to open is position_size * mark_price / leverage.

maintenance_margin_rate.note: Half the initial margin rate at the tier's max leverage; 2.5% at 20x.

maintenance_deduction.note: maintenance_margin = notional * maintenance_margin_rate - maintenance_deduction. Margin tables with IDs below 50 have one tier with max leverage equal to the ID.

mainnet_tiers.note: Mainnet margin tiers by notional position value. The page gives the upper tier as '>' the bound.

liquidation_price.formula: price - side * margin_available / position_size / (1 - side / maintenance_leverage)
liquidation_price.note: side = 1 long, -1 short. margin_available = account_value - maintenance_margin_required (cross) or isolated_margin - maintenance_margin_required (isolated).

backstop_threshold.note: Backstop liquidation when account equity drops below 2/3 of maintenance margin.

threshold.note: Positions larger than this get partial market liquidation orders (10k USDC on testnet).

rate_8h.note: The formula gives an 8-hour rate; premium_index is the hourly average of 5-second premium samples.

rate_hourly.note: Funding is paid every hour at one eighth of the computed rate, capped at 0.5%/hour.

cap_per_hour.note: The funding cap and funding interval do not depend on the asset.

payment.note: Uses the spot oracle price, not the mark price. Positive rate: longs pay shorts.

expiry.note: Delivery / expiration: N/A (funding payments every hour). Position limit: N/A.

oracle.note: USDC collateral on USDT-denominated linear contracts, no USDC/USDT conversion (quanto). PURR-USD and HYPE-USD are USDC-denominated.

margin_modes.note: Cross is the default. Strict isolated: margin cannot be removed. HIP-3 DEXs also support no-cross mode.

fee_scale.note: Validator-operated perps use the base fee tiers.
From the page's fee formula for developers (scaleIfHip3).

growth_mode_scale.note: Growth mode cuts protocol fees, rebates and volume contributions by 90%; deployer fee scale must be 0 to 10.

taker_fee.note: Inputs: N, deployer_fee_scale, growth_mode (1 or 0), tier=. Excludes staking, referral and aligned-quote adjustments.

settlement.note: The deployer may settle with haltTrading, which cancels orders and settles positions at the current mark price. Deployers set oracle prices and leverage limits.

model_fee.unverified: Fee formula and coefficient are on the Kalshi fee schedule, which was not readable here. The fee rounding page's worked example (model fee $0.00363825 for 1 contract at $0.055) is consistent with 0.07 x C x P x (1 - P).

trade_fee.note: Trade fee is the model fee rounded up to six decimal places.

fee.formula: ceil_to(C * P + trade_fee, fees.rounding.balance_step) - C * P
fee.note: Total fee on one buy fill of C contracts at price P: trade fee plus rounding fee, where the balance change is floored to the member's balance precision. Excludes the per-order accumulator and rebates.

model_fee.unverified: Maker fee formula and the series it applies to are on the Kalshi fee schedule, which was not readable here.

multiplier.note: August 22, 2026 entry: "The maker fee uses a fee multiplier of `0.5`, rather than the standard `0.25`." The 0.5 applies to the quoter fee swap.

trade_fee.note: Trade fee is the model fee rounded up to six decimal places.

fee.formula: ceil_to(C * P + trade_fee, fees.rounding.balance_step) - C * P
fee.note: Same rounding as the taker fee; the rounding rule covers every fill, maker or taker.

balance_step.note: Non-direct member balances are aligned to $0.01. Pass balance_step=0.0001 for a direct member.

balance_step_direct.note: Direct member balances are aligned to $0.0001.

accumulator.note: Rounding overpayment accumulates per order across all fills, maker or taker, and is rebated in balance-precision steps.

net_fee_floor.note: Net fee = trade fee + rounding fee - rebate, never below zero.

price_decimals.note: *_dollars price fields carry up to 4 decimal places.

source_of_truth.note: Each market's price_ranges is the source of truth for valid prices; price_level_structure is only a label.

structures.note: Bands as described on the page; the page does not say which band owns a boundary price. step.note: Minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts; inputs accept 0 to 2 decimal places.

max_leverage.note: Each market has a leverage tier schedule (from Market Data); larger positions must run at lower leverage. The numbers are not on the margin page.

initial_margin.note: IM = Notional / Leverage, at your configured leverage, which applies to the whole notional.

maintenance_margin_rate.note: MMR = 0.5 / MaxLeverage, flat per market, independent of position size, tier and leverage setting; 2.5% on a 20x market.

maintenance_margin.note: MM = Notional x MMR. Liquidation begins when equity falls below MM.

interval_hours.note: Premium samples are averaged over the 1-hour charge window and the hourly rate is settled once at its end.

impact_notional.note: Quote notional each side of the book is walked for to get bid_impact and ask_impact; a side that cannot fill it falls back to Index.

rate_8h.note: premium_index is the mean of the window's samples; scale is asset_classes.crypto.funding_scale or asset_classes.other.funding_scale.

rate_hourly.note: Positive: longs pay shorts. Funding is a direct transfer between longs and shorts; the protocol takes no cut.

interest_rate_8h.note: Fixed interest leg of 0.01% per 8 hours.

reference.unverified: Index and mark price rules are in Polymarket's perps docs, not readable here.

margin_mode.note: Isolated is the default when neither you nor your account group set a mode. Switching needs no position and no open orders in that market.

funding_scale.note: Every market that is not crypto.

overrides.unverified: Other differences between crypto and other markets, if any, are in Polymarket's perps FAQ, not readable here.
